pages.text:
Morgan Stanley (2 Month Internship) On-Campus 
 
I. 
Coding Round (only for TY CS and IT) conducted on AMCAT 
 
1. Aptitude (10 question and 20min) 
It had Quantitative Aptitude questions (to prepare for this you can use indiabix.com  or 
javatpoint.com) 
 
2.  Code Debugging 7 ques (20mins) 
(Some easy codes like find max product of 3 numbers, find median, find the smallest 
distance, area of triangle, loops) 
3. Coding (3 questions 1 hour) 
a. It was too long and something related to priority, I didn't attempt it all 
b. Find the number with maximum number of 1's in binary from a given set of numbers. 
(I missed just one test case for this, probably due to modulo) 
c. The question was based on disjoint set (union-find), I don't exactly remember the 
question. It said there are a given number of people with priority assigned to each, and 
some groups already made. Some requirements were given. You've to find out the first 
batch of people that can work simultaneously with highest priority. (Only passed 1 test 
case and time was up) 
The questions were too long, and little confusing to understand (so I would suggest read all 
the questions, understand it, and start with the one you know the logic of) 
 
Out of all 26 were selected for the next round (Interview) 
 
II. 
Interview 1: Technical Round (1-hour 15mins) 
→ Tell me about yourself (expected technical stuff) 
→ Which programming language do you use? I said C++. A few questions about Base and 
Derived class pointers, virtual keyword, will base classes static member be available to 
derived class. (trial and error a program to learn, when what is inherited) 
→ Linked List: Given a set of numbers, find the greatest element up to (took me a little 
time to understand the question) 
Example: 1,3,5,10,7,8,3 
Output: 10,10,10,10,8,8,3 
I was asked to explain the approach, after that optimize it (which I didn't), coded it on 
notepad.  
After that I was asked to convert it into Recursive solution, only partly I could. 
→ Given a huge file, and size of RAM is less, how will your sort it?

Ans: External Merge Sort (https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/external-sorting/) /Min Heap 
Approach, then if there are duplicates will the order be maintained (which sort has that 
property? Merge, Quick or Heap, Ans: Merge) 
→ Some array questions, convert the array into low-high-low-high points 
Example: 1,5,6,7,8,9 
Output:5,1,7,6,9,8 
→ OS Questions: 
o Deadlock Conditions? 
o What if RAM is overloaded? 
o Booting process 
o Few fellow interviewees were asked about thread, process and multithreading 
intensively  
 
Out of 26 only 10 were shortlisted 
 
III. Interview 2: HR+Technical (1:30 hour) 
→ Gave me 7-10mins to explain about myself and how I got into Tech, asked me about 
how do I related my extra-curricular activities to the academic stuff (be true, don't fake 
around, it doesn’t help the vibe) 
→ Asked me to rank myself among my peers and why? 
→  If I've had read any technical books, learnt any language out of the way (I was true to 
say NO and which he appreciated)  
→ One thing in your attitude, you would like to give your peers and one you want to take 
from them. 
Tip: BE TRUE 
→ Technical Part: Design an Uber Lite (give all the entities, how will they communicate 
using OOPs concept), lasted an hour. 
 
8/10 were selected for the internship (It was decided before the last undisclosed round) 
 
IV. There was another round. But let's keep that a secret xD. 
 
Tips to work on: 
1. Archives on GFG (go through every single one for the company, there is a pattern ;) ) 
2. GFG for data structures 
3. OS (Deadlock, Process Synchronization, CPU Scheduling, Threads, Memory-RAM) 
4. DBMS (Normalisation and SQL Queries)
